chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud Al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

How many are deceived by what Allah has bestowed upon him, and how many are gradually allured by Allah's veiling (of His punishment) upon him, and how many are captivated by the praise of people for him.

key_terms.أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: Allah has bestowed favor upon him

ai.seo_question: What are the three ways people are spiritually deceived according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) as a concise taxonomy of spiritual deception, distinguishing between the passive trap of blessings (ni'mah), the subtle danger of divine concealment (satr) where punishment is delayed, and the active allure of social validation. This triad underscores the Shia ethical emphasis on maintaining inner vigilance (muraqabah) against both external comforts and internal pride, warning that ease often precedes downfall.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood Al Minqary, from Hafs Bin Giyas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘How many are proud due to what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favoured upon him, and how many are gradually allured by the Veiling of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon him, and how many are infatuated by the praises of the people upon him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman (ibn Dawud) al-Minqari from Hafs ibn Ghiyath from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

How many are those who suffer losses due to the bounties that Allah grant them! How many are those who gradually move to destruction due to Allah’s covering their sins! How many are of the people misled due to other’s prais and applause for them!”’
